errors: No mathematical errors. The symbol μ is overloaded: it denotes both the number of nodes and the dimension functions μ(g,ν), μ(Σ), μ(δ,Σ). The usage is nonetheless consistent.
Condition (e) together with (f) gives exactly the usual stability condition 2g_δ−2+ν_δ>0 for each vertex, once the trivial case (g=1, ν=0) is excluded as he notes.

ideas.what: Encoding a stable pointed curve by a combinatorial datum: vertices = components with genus labels, half-edges = preimages of nodes, legs = marked points, plus connectedness, genus formula and stability conditions
ideas.modern_name: stable graph / dual graph of a stable curve (modular graph)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford 1969, Knudsen 1983; formalised as stable/modular graphs by Kontsevich, Getzler–Kapranov, Arbarello–Cornalba
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the stratification of \bar M_{g,ν} by combinatorial types and the Teichmüller tower; detailed axioms unsure

ideas.what: Dimension of the stratum of type Σ equals Σ_δ (3g_δ−3+ν_δ) = 3g−3+ν − (number of nodes)
ideas.modern_name: codimension of boundary stratum = number of edges of the stable graph
ideas.where_published: implicit in Esquisse d'un programme's description of the boundary strata of modular multiplicities

deep.surprise_reason: A clean and correct but standard combinatorial set-up of stable graphs and the dimension count for boundary strata. It was well known by 1981 and appears in all later treatments; the only distinctive feature is Grothendieck's categorical phrasing (a pushout for connectedness, a degree-2 map for edges).

'D = (par abus de notation) ens. des pts doubles' rather than '(par une notation[?])'.
Condition a): 'D ⊔_{\tilde D} Δ de card. 1' (cardinality 1, i.e. connected), not 'de conn. 1'.
